developments.facts: Reuters Asian report associates US-centric AI stress with Treasury demand, lower yields and a softer/subdued dollar. AP reports deep Japan/Korea technology-share weakness alongside firmer Australia/Hong Kong, limiting claims of a uniform regional collapse. Earlier October 29 two-year yield decline stays dated background. FX haven/funding transmission is inference, not observed carry liquidation or private flows.

developments.title: RBNZ hold surprise and subsequent hawkish offset
developments.facts: The complete official October 28 record confirms a 4-3 hold at 2.75%, against widely expected October tightening. The majority cited lower-than -expected inflation, smaller indirect fuel-price effects, subdued wages, weak consumption/investment and time to observe two previous hikes. Core near the upper target band and broader price increases were largely expected, rather than evidence of a fresh upside surprise. All members still see tighter policy likely, conditional on the outlook; the record explicitly allows future holds or easing if global demand deteriorates sharply. RNZ reports Westpac economist Eckhold observed the one-year swap rate down about 20 bp after the decision on October 28. That report is an attributed event-time observation, not a new/current October 29 yield measurement. Later conference remarks about further hikes and imported inflation are substantial opposition to weakness. The October 29 Herald interview is now verified separately; this does not verify every scheduled broadcast. Wholesale-to-retail rate pass-through and cost-to-CPI pass-through are distinct; no mechanical rate conclusion is drawn from either.
